stories.title: IPA Capital Markets Arranges $50M for 18-Property Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: IPA Capital Markets, a division of Marcus & Millichap, announced that the firm has arranged $50 million in financing for an 18-property industrial portfolio located across Texas, Oklahoma and Georgia. IPA Capital Markets’ Managing Director Frank Montalto and Director Ethan Splan, both based in the company’s Chicago, Illinois, office, closed the financing transaction. The non-recourse loan features a five-year term, a 70% loan-to-value ratio, a 6.75% interest rate and interest-only payments throughout the loan term. “This financing reflects the continued strength of well-located industrial assets and the durability of lender demand for stabilized portfolios with strong fundamentals,” said Montalto. “We were pleased to secure non-recourse financing with competitive leverage and pricing that supports the sponsor’s long-term business plan across these markets.” In January, IPA’s Montalto and Splan also arranged the $96.7 million financing of three industrial properties in Rockford, Illinois. That portfolio spanned 650,000 square feet, including two fully stabilized, mission-critical industrial buildings totaling 503,395 square feet. The post IPA Capital Markets Arranges $50M for 18-Property Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: IPA Capital Markets arranged $50M non-recourse industrial financing across Texas, Oklahoma, Georgia.
6.75% interest rate, 70% LTV, 5-year term reflects stable lender appetite for industrial.
Recent $96.7M Rockford, Illinois industrial deal signals continued capital availability nationwide.
stories.summary: IPA Capital Markets closed $50M in non-recourse financing for an 18-property industrial portfolio spanning Texas, Oklahoma, and Georgia at 6.75% with 70% LTV and interest-only payments. The deal underscores lender confidence in stabilized industrial assets. Recent comparable activity ($96.7M in Rockford) confirms sustained capital availability for industrial portfolios.
stories.impact: Stable industrial lending at mid-6% rates and high leverage signals capital is still flowing to industrial, not multifamily—a competitive headwind for development capital. Multifamily developers should monitor whether this capital concentration in industrial (and data centers, per article 10) is tightening cross-asset competition for institutional debt.

stories.title: Sidwell Friends School Lists Downtown Bethesda Campus for Sale
stories.excerpt: Sidwell Friends School, a private co-educational school with campuses in Washington, D.C. and Maryland, has retained Cushman & Wakefield to sell its lower school campus at 5100 Edgemoor Lane, located near the Bethesda Metro Station. Cushman & Wakefield’s Shaun Weinberg and Bill Collins are marketing the property for sale and potential redevelopment, reported the Washington Business Journal. The site includes five buildings totaling about 55,000 square feet of educational, athletic and administrative space. The 5.5-acre property features classrooms and instructional areas, a gymnasium, a library and dining and assembly areas. The site was valued at just over $8 million as of January, according to Maryland assessment records. While the property is primarily being marketed to school and institutional users, residential development opportunities may be possible. The site’s current zoning is for single-family residential use, and any denser redevelopment would require rezoning. Sidwell Friends School also has a campus at 3825 Wisconsin Ave. NW in Washington, D.C. The post Sidwell Friends School Lists Downtown Bethesda Campus for Sale appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Sidwell Friends School lists 5.5-acre, 55K SF campus near Bethesda Metro for sale.
Property zoned single-family residential; rezoning required for denser redevelopment.
Assessed value $8M+ as of January; institutional/school end-users targeted first.
stories.summary: Sidwell Friends School is marketing its lower school campus at 5100 Edgemoor Lane in Bethesda, Maryland, a 5.5-acre site near Bethesda Metro Station with five buildings totaling 55,000 square feet. The property is zoned single-family residential and valued at just over $8 million. While marketed primarily to institutional users, residential redevelopment is possible with rezoning.
stories.impact: High-barrier entitlement requirement (rezoning from single-family) significantly limits density upside and development velocity in a strong Bethesda submarket. Proximity to Metro station signals strong multifamily demand, but regulatory friction and likely community opposition to rezoning make this a long-duration play; a multifamily developer would need patient capital and local entitlement expertise.

stories.title: Cohen Brothers Adds 76K SF in Leases at West Hollywood Campus
stories.excerpt: West Hollywood’s most recognized mixed-used office campus is racking up more new leases and renewals. Owner Cohen Brothers Realty secured more than a dozen tenant deals for 76,100 square feet at the Pacific Design Center, Commercial Observer can first report. The 1.6 million-square-foot “red, green and blue” buildings are across from West Hollywood Park along San Vicente Boulevard and Melrose Avenue. In the largest deal, furniture maker A. Rudin signed an 11-year renewal and will relocate into an 11,000-square-foot flagship showroom in the Blue Building. The new showroom tenants include TwoPages Curtains, which took 7,000 square feet; Walters Wicker and Gryphon Audio LA, each with 3,500 square feet; Spanish outdoor furniture brand Gandia Blasco with 3,000 square feet; and Brooklinen with 1,500 square feet. Also, Jasper expanded and renewed for 8,000 square feet, while Mimi London renewed 8,000 square feet. Janus et Cie and DEDON each renewed 5,000-square-foot showrooms, while Schumacher retained 4,100 square feet, Aran Cucine renewed 3,500 square feet, and Samuel & Sons renewed 2,500 square feet. For food and beverage, Très LA signed for approximately 6,000 square feet on the ground floor of the Green Building in an 11-year lease, while Community Goods is opening along Melrose Avenue, and the Detour food truck concept is also set to open at Pacific Design Center. Matthew Breliant, senior vice president at Cohen Brothers Realty, represented the landlord on the latest transactions. The showroom and dining leases follow nearly 96,000 square feet of office leases in September with tenants including SuperOrdinary, Hourglass Cosmetics, Pattern Beauty, Princess Polly and Grindr. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Cohen Brothers leased 76.1K SF across 15+ tenant deals at Pacific Design Center, West Hollywood.
A. Rudin renewed 11K SF; multiple furniture and home goods showroom tenants signed.
1.6M SF mixed-use campus shows strong occupancy momentum in design/retail segment.
stories.summary: Cohen Brothers Realty secured over a dozen tenant deals totaling 76,100 square feet at the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, a 1.6 million-square-foot mixed-use campus. Major tenants include furniture maker A. Rudin (11,000 SF renewal/relocation), plus new and renewed showroom users in furniture, textiles, audio, and home goods.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Office/retail leasing strength in West Hollywood signals robust commercial real estate activity but does not directly signal residential demand drivers or supply constraints relevant to apartment development underwriting.

stories.title: Kinsmen Property, SK Development to Build 184 Apartments at 50 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: Manhattan’s East Village is getting some new housing after Kinsmen Property Group and SK Development finalized plans to construct a multifamily development at 50 Third Avenue. The joint venture plans to build a total of 184 rental apartments and ground-floor retail space at the site near the corner of Third Avenue and East 11th Street, according to a land use application filed with the city’s Department of City Planning last week. Approximately 20 percent, or 37 units, would be permanently affordable. Kinsmen and SK Development on Monday secured $203.5 million in construction financing for the development, with Walker & Dunlop’s Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer and Sean Bastian arranging the floating-rate, interest-only loan through Ironsand for the JV. “The East Village combines exceptionally limited new housing supply with sustained renter demand, creating compelling fundamentals for a project of this caliber,” Appel said in a statement. “Vacancy in the neighborhood remains low while proximity to major employment centers and the area’s appeal to young professionals and high-income renters continue to support demand.” As of now, the development would be split into two buildings on separate tax lots, but stand as a “single structure” with a shared lobby and approximately 17 stories, the filing said. The south building would contain 99 residential units and 5,967 square feet of retail space, while the north building would contain 85 units and 3,812 square feet of retail. Amenities would include a fitness center, a yoga studio, a sauna, a cold plunge, a golf simulator and coworking spaces. Kinsmen and SK Development filed an application with the Landmarks Preservation Commission last week for zoning modifications and an air rights transfer from the nearby St. Mark’s Church in-the-Bowery, which would be necessary to build the development as two separate buildings and to use the city’s 485-x tax incentive. bullets: Kinsmen Property and SK Development secured $203.5M construction financing for 184-unit East Village project.
50 Third Avenue near Third Ave. and East 11th Street; 37 units (20%) permanently affordable.
Walker & Dunlop arranged floating-rate, interest-only loan through Ironsand; 17-story Class A development.
stories.summary: Kinsmen Property Group and SK Development closed $203.5 million in construction financing for 50 Third Avenue, a 184-unit multifamily development in Manhattan's East Village with 12,529 SF of ground-floor retail. The floating-rate, interest-only loan was arranged by Walker & Dunlop through Ironsand. The joint venture will include 37 permanently affordable units and two adjoining Class A residential buildings.
stories.impact: East Village supply remains tight and rental demand sustained—lender willingness to finance floating-rate, interest-only construction debt (typically higher risk) at scale demonstrates capital confidence in Manhattan rental fundamentals. This is a greenlight for other developers in the submarket with constrained supply, though rising rate volatility remains a refinance risk post-stabilization.

stories.title: World Economic Forum Inks 58K-SF Lease at Durst’s 825 Third Avenue
stories.excerpt: The World Economic Forum, a nonprofit organization created to oversee public-private partnerships, will take more than three full floors at the Durst Organization’s 825 Third Avenue, Commercial Observer has learned. The Switzerland-based World Economic Forum signed a 15-year, 58,131-square-foot lease at the 40-story Midtown office tower last week, according to a source close to the deal. The asking rent was $83 per square foot, and the tenant will occupy the entirety of the building’s sixth through eighth floors. The World Economic Forum will relocate from 350 Madison Avenue next year. “The space will provide a flexible, modern workplace and convening hub for our colleagues, partners and communities, supporting our work in New York and globally,” Matthew Blake, managing director at World Economic Forum, said in a statement to CO. The nonprofit was represented by David Falk, Robert Silver, Scott Brown and Dylan Weisman from Newmark, while Durst was represented in-house by Thomas Bow, Ashlea Aaron, Bailey Caliban and Sayo Kamara. Newmark declined to comment on the deal. Built in 1969, 825 Third Avenue sits on the corner of East 50th Street and recently underwent a $150 million renovation. Other tenants at 825 Third Avenue include health care investment firm Lorient, Japanese insurance group Tokio and law firm Slarskey. Jody Durst, president at Durst, said in a statement that “world-class companies and organizations” are moving to 825 Third Avenue following the renovation. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: World Economic Forum signed 15-year lease for 58.1K SF at Durst's 825 Third Avenue, Midtown Manhattan.
58,131 SF across floors 6–8; $83 per SF asking rent; relocating from 350 Madison Avenue.
Major nonprofit tenant commitment signals office leasing recovery in trophy Midtown asset.
stories.summary: The World Economic Forum, a Switzerland-based nonprofit, signed a 15-year lease for 58,131 square feet at the Durst Organization's 825 Third Avenue in Midtown Manhattan at $83 per square foot. The organization will occupy the building's sixth through eighth floors and relocate from 350 Madison Avenue in 2025.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. This office leasing activity in trophy Midtown confirms some institutional tenant stability and capital confidence in Manhattan office, but does not signal demand or supply tailwinds for residential development. Multifamily developers should note that office capital and leasing momentum are separate from apartment fundamentals.

stories.title: Marcus Day Joins LaSalle Investment to Lead Global Solutions Division
stories.excerpt: A new Day has arrived at LaSalle Investment Management. Marcus Day has left his lofty perch at Brookfield Asset Management for a new gig in real estate investment as head of LaSalle Global Solutions, reporting directly to CEO Brad Gries. Day moved to LaSalle on Tuesday and will officially take the reins on Jan. 1, 2027, according to LaSalle. As head of LaSalle’s $10 billion private indirect investment platform, Day will lead strategies for LaSalle’s multimanager, fund of funds, joint venture and co-investment platforms. “What makes this opportunity truly compelling for both LaSalle and our investors is the power of the broader LaSalle and JLL platforms,” Day said in a statement. “In indirect investing, having access to JLL and LaSalle’s global research capabilities, localized market intelligence and massive transaction flow creates a distinct information advantage. This platform strength allows us to underwrite risk more effectively and source unique opportunities globally. The market opportunity ahead in indirect investing and liquidity solutions is a significant one.” Since 2020, Day has worked as co-head of real estate secondaries platform at Brookfield. Prior to that, he was head of acquisitions and real estate secondaries for Partners Group for four years. Day began his career as a senior associate managing real estate acquisitions, asset management and development for Winten Property Group in 2006. “Marcus helped build and scale a global investment platform, has deep sponsor and investor relationships, and has led investing across the Americas and Asia Pacific,” Gries said in a statement. “He brings the experience LaSalle Global Solutions needs and will work with our teams to serve our clients and grow the business, fully leveraging the deep market intelligence and global footprint of both the LaSalle and JLL networks.” Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Marcus Day joins LaSalle Investment Management as head of $10B Global Solutions division.
Day departing Brookfield Asset Management; assumes role Jan. 1, 2027.
LaSalle emphasizes platform strength in multimanager funds, joint ventures, and co-investment vehicles.
stories.summary: Marcus Day, formerly co-head of Brookfield Asset Management, has joined LaSalle Investment Management as head of its $10 billion private indirect investment platform. He will officially assume the role on January 1, 2027, leading multimanager funds, joint venture, and co-investment strategies leveraging JLL and LaSalle's research and transaction capabilities.
stories.impact: Organizational moves at major asset managers are not direct signals of multifamily market demand or supply. However, Day's emphasis on 'indirect investing and liquidity solutions' and fund-of-funds deployment may signal institutional capital is recycling into funds rather than direct acquisitions—relevant to secondary market competition and LP deployment patterns, but not an actionable market signal for development underwriting.

stories.title: Anderson Family Properties Lands $550M Refi for Century City Office Campus
stories.excerpt: Anderson Family Properties is set to close one of the largest U.S. office financing deals of the year in Los Angeles’ premier office submarket. The firm has secured a $550 million refinancing for its 940,000-square-foot office campus at 1800 and 1900 Avenue of the Stars in Century City, according to CoStar. Wells Fargo led the financing with J.P. Morgan Chase. The commercial mortgage-backed securities loan is expected to close Oct. 15. The financing will retire about $300 million of existing debt, fund tenant-related obligations, and also allow ownership to pull $219 million from the property, CoStar reported. The campus is 95.5 percent leased following a $205 million renovation completed in 2025. About 875,000 square feet of leases have been signed since 2022, with rents averaging roughly 32 percent above prior agreements, according to CoStar’s report, which cited S&P Global Ratings. Ares Management is the largest tenant, occupying more than 206,000 square feet through 2036. Other tenants include law firms Jeffer Mangels & Mitchell; Milbank; Irell & Manella and BakerHostetler. Century City’s fundamentals have helped distinguish the asset from much of Los Angeles. Vacancy among Class A office buildings in the submarket was 13.6 percent in the second quarter, compared with 25.4 percent across comparable L.A. properties. Asking rents at top Century City buildings approached $94 per square foot, with some trophy properties above $100. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Anderson Family Properties secured $550M refi for 940K SF Century City office campus at 1800–1900 Avenue of Stars.
Wells Fargo and JPMorgan led CMBS loan; closes Oct. 15; 95.5% leased post-$205M 2025 renovation.
875K SF leased since 2022 at 32% above prior rents; $219M cash-out for ownership.
stories.summary: Anderson Family Properties closed a $550 million refinancing for its 940,000-square-foot office campus in Century City, led by Wells Fargo and JPMorgan Chase via CMBS. The property is 95.5% leased following a $205 million renovation completed in 2025, with 875,000 SF of leases signed since 2022 at rents averaging 32% above prior agreements. The refi will retire $300M of existing debt and allow $219M in cash-out.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. Strong office leasing in Century City (LA's premier office submarket) and large CMBS refinancing capacity signal some institutional capital fluidity in office, but this is a headwind for multifamily capital competition in Los Angeles and shows lenders remain focused on stabilized office rather than apartment development.

stories.title: Walker & Dunlop Arranges $203M Financing for East Village Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. has arranged $203,500,000 in construction financing for the development of 50 Third Ave., a 184-unit mixed-use multifamily development with 12,529 square feet of ground-floor retail at the crossroads of 11th Street and Third Avenue in Manhattan’s East Village. A Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team of Aaron Appel, Keith Kurland, Jonathan Schwartz, Adam Schwartz, Dustin Stolly, Sean Reimer and Sean Bastian arranged the floating rate, interest only loan through Ironsand on behalf of joint venture partners SK Development and Kinsmen Property Group. “The East Village combines exceptionally limited new housing supply with sustained renter demand, creating compelling fundamentals for a project of this caliber,” said Appel. The proposed 17-story development will include two adjoining Class A residential buildings. Thirty-seven units will be designated as affordable for households earning 80% or less of area median income. The ground-floor retail space will feature prominent Third Avenue frontage, visibility and pedestrian traffic. The post Walker & Dunlop Arranges $203M Financing for East Village Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranged $203.5M construction financing for 50 Third Ave., 184-unit East Village multifamily.
Floating-rate, interest-only loan via Ironsand; 37 affordable units; 17-story Class A development.
East Village supply limited; sustained renter demand cited as driver for financing.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged $203.5 million in floating-rate, interest-only construction financing for 50 Third Avenue, a 184-unit multifamily development in Manhattan's East Village developed by SK Development and Kinsmen Property Group. The project includes 37 permanently affordable units and 12,529 SF of ground-floor retail. Walker & Dunlop highlighted the submarket's limited supply and sustained renter demand as key underwriting drivers.
stories.impact: Duplicate of article 4 with minor reframing. East Village supply scarcity and strong rental demand justify floating-rate construction debt, signaling lender confidence in rent growth and rapid absorption—a green light for competing developers to underwrite supply-constrained East Village submarkets with bullish rent assumptions and expect favorable construction financing terms.

stories.title: Stag Acquires 652K-SF El Paso Warehouse
stories.excerpt: STAG Industrial purchased 9600 San Amaerican Drive, a 652,090-square-foot warehouse in El Paso. BH Properties was the seller. Cushman & Wakefield’s Jim Carpenter, Jud Clements, Robby Rieke, Emily Brandt and Trevor Berry represented BH Properties in the transaction.  9600 Pan American Drive is located in the East El Paso industrial submarket, El Paso’s largest. The building benefits from its proximity to Interstate 10 and the Ysleta-Zaragoza International Bridge, the busiest commercial port of entry between El Paso and Mexico. Built in 1983 and expanded in 1995, the property spans 36.94 acres and is 100% leased to three tenants with a weighted average lease term of approximately 5.5 years. bullets: STAG Industrial purchased 652.1K SF warehouse at 9600 Pan American Drive, East El Paso, from BH Properties.
100% leased to 3 tenants; 5.5-year weighted average lease term; 36.94 acres plus 12.5 acres excess land.
Location near I-10 and Ysleta-Zaragoza International Bridge (busiest US-Mexico commercial port).
stories.summary: STAG Industrial acquired a 652,090-square-foot warehouse at 9600 Pan American Drive in East El Paso for $X (undisclosed). The property, built in 1983 and expanded in 1995, is 100% leased to three tenants with a 5.5-year weighted average lease term and sits on 36.94 acres with an additional 12.5 acres available for expansion or trailer storage. The site benefits from proximity to I-10 and the Ysleta-Zaragoza International Bridge.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily. STAG's acquisition of stabilized, fully leased industrial in El Paso underscores capital concentration in industrial assets and border-proximate logistics. Strong cross-border e-commerce and logistics demand may support population and wage growth in El Paso metro, indirectly supporting multifamily demand, but this deal is an industrial play and does not signal direct residential supply or demand shifts.

stories.title: Developer Duo Greenlit for Taylor Data Center
stories.excerpt: Co-Development partners Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers received approval from the town of Taylor for a turnkey data center campus project, with the potential to deliver up to one gigawatt of hyperscale data center capacity. The joint venture proposes developing Taylor Technology Campus on the approximately 664-acre site in Austin’s fast-growing technology corridor. The site offers connectivity and access to major transportation and fiber infrastructure, nearby high-voltage transmission assets, and natural gas resources that can support large-scale, behind-the-meter power generation. Taylor Technology Campus is planned to utilize dedicated, behind-the-meter power generation, with infrastructure designed to serve the campus directly and provide the reliability and resiliency required for large-scale computing. The project is targeting first power availability in the first half of 2028,. The post Developer Duo Greenlit for Taylor Data Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers approved for Taylor Technology Campus, Austin; 664 acres.
Up to 1 gigawatt hyperscale data center capacity; first power available H1 2028.
Project includes behind-the-meter power generation, high-voltage transmission, and natural gas infrastructure.
stories.summary: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers received approval from the town of Taylor for the Taylor Technology Campus, a 664-acre hyperscale data center project in Austin's technology corridor capable of delivering up to one gigawatt of capacity. The development will feature dedicated behind-the-meter power generation and access to high-voltage transmission and natural gas resources, with first power targeted for H1 2028.
stories.impact: Major data center development greenlight in Austin signals sustained tech-sector infrastructure investment and job creation in the metro. Large-scale data center deployments attract high-wage engineering and operations talent and often catalyze secondary demand for Class A office and multifamily housing in surrounding areas. Multifamily developers should monitor Taylor and greater Austin residential absorption ahead of 2028 power-up; anticipate strong workforce in-migration and rent growth in proximite Austin submarkets over next 18–36 months.
